D001808.s: Any of the tubular vessels conveying the blood (arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules, and veins).

D001901.s: The study of the origin, structure, development, growth, function, genetics, and reproduction of plants.

D002306.s: The volume of the heart, usually relating to the volume of blood contained within it at various periods of the cardiac cycle. The amount of blood ejected from a ventricle at each beat is stroke volume.

D002423.s: Factors which produce cessation of all vital bodily functions. They can be analyzed from an epidemiologic viewpoint.

D002647.s: Recurrent localized itching, swelling and painful erythema on the fingers, toes or ears, produced by exposure to cold.

D003015.s: Infections with bacteria of the genus clostridium and closely related clostridioides or reclassified members of Clostridium.

D003745.s: The property of dental enamel to permit passage of light, heat, gases, liquids, metabolites, mineral ions and other substances. It does not include the penetration of the dental enamel by microorganisms.

D004032.s: Regular course of eating and drinking adopted by a person or animal.

D007428.s: Skin tests in which the sensitizer is injected.

D007802.s: A verbal or nonverbal means of communicating ideas or feelings.

D009080.s: An acute, febrile, mucocutaneous condition accompanied by swelling of cervical lymph nodes in infants and young children.

D009422.s: Diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. This includes disorders of the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, peripheral nerves, nerve roots, autonomic nervous system, neuromuscular junction, and muscle.

D009956.s: Infection with chlamydophila psittaci (formerly Chlamydia psittaci), transmitted to humans by inhalation of dust-borne contaminated nasal secretions or excreta of infected birds. This infection results in a febrile illness characterized by pneumonitis and systemic manifestations.

D013090.s: Male germ cells derived from spermatogonia. The euploid primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis and give rise to the haploid secondary spermatocytes which in turn give rise to spermatids.

D013216.s: A complex involuntary response to an unexpected strong stimulus. The reaction involves physical movement away from the stimulus, muscle contraction and limb flexion, blinking, and changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and respiration.

D013582.s: The clear, viscous fluid secreted by the synovial membrane. It contains mucin, albumin, fat, and mineral salts and serves to lubricate joints.

D013920.s: A clinical syndrome characterized by repeated spontaneous hemorrhages and a remarkable increase in the number of circulating platelets.

D014389.s: Mycobacterium infections of the male reproductive tract (genitalia, male).

D014774.s: The degree of pathogenicity within a group or species of microorganisms or viruses as indicated by case fatality rates and/or the ability of the organism to invade the tissues of the host. The pathogenic capacity of an organism is determined by its virulence factors.

D016387.s: The concept covering the physical and mental conditions of women.

D016857.s: Clinical manifestation consisting of a deficiency of carbon dioxide in arterial blood.

D018433.s: Works about methods of detecting genetic etiology in human traits. The basic premise of twin studies is that monozygotic twins carry identical genes, while zygotic twins are genetically no more similar than two siblings born after separate pregnancies.

D040362.s: Computer systems capable of assembling, storing, manipulating, and displaying geographically referenced information, i.e. data identified according to their locations.

D044483.s: The growth of intestinal polyps. Growth processes include neoplastic (adenoma and carcinoma) and non-neoplastic (hyperplastic, mucosal, inflammatory, and other polyps).

D054712.s: Degree of saltiness, which is largely the osmolar concentration of sodium chloride plus any other salts present. It is an ecological factor of considerable importance, influencing the types of organisms that live in an environment.

D055665.s: A severe, rapidly fatal reaction occurring most commonly in children following an infectious illness. It is characterized by large, rapidly spreading skin hemorrhages, fever, or shock. Purpura fulminans often accompanies or is triggered by disseminated intravascular coagulation.

D057872.s: Materials used in dental pulp capping or pulpectomy.

D066263.s: A biochemical phenomenon in which misfolded proteins aggregate either intra- or extracellularly.

D000077230.s: Ability to connect to access services available on the Internet.

D000081028.s: Damage to the eye or its function (e.g., visual impairment) due to optic nerve damage secondary to toxic substances such as drugs used in chemotherapy; immunotherapy; or radiation.
